parsed.explanation: The combined regime pairs a protective division with a hostile national layer the traveller cannot avoid. Universal exposures apply: entry officers are instructed to refuse visas where documents cast doubt on sex and to weigh lifetime fraud ineligibility; X markers are barred and passports blocked; a national order bars trans people from government-funded single-sex facilities everywhere, with 21 states adding school/building bans and 4 allowing criminal charges (one arrest, held 24h in a men's ward). Custody is worse: a conversion-therapy mandate in national corrections and documented beatings, solitary and sexual abuse in immigration custody. Mitigation is real but partial — enjoined orders, shield laws, a protective division, hate-crime statute — and litigation leaves outcomes contingent.

entry_documents.exposure: Feb 2025 cable tells officers to refuse cases where documents or records cast reasonable doubt on sex and to consider lifetime fraud ineligibility; X markers barred, new passports M/F only; travellers report passports blocked/confiscated, some stranded; eight-plus foreign governments issued advisories.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X-marker passports valid to expiry; fraud finding requires four elements with limited waiver and is never automatic; ACLU suit pending; legal-aid FAQ on document rules.
entry_documents.interaction: Entry rules are national and override any division shield; document mismatch can escalate into fraud allegation then detention.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: From 2026 national corrections mandate conversion therapy (hair cut, hormones removed, psychiatric substitution); transgender immigration detainees report forced labour, beatings, solitary and severe sexual abuse; division prison used birth-sex transfer as discipline (Jul 2024); trans woman held 24h in men's ward after bathroom arrest.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Division courts have required gender-affirming care in its prisons since Oct 2023; several national orders enjoined; national hate-crime statute covers gender identity.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: A visitor detained federally or in immigration custody never reaches the division's prison protections.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: National order bars trans people from government-funded single-sex facilities; equality map (7 Nov 2026): 9+1 states cover all government buildings, 9 more schools plus buildings, 3 schools only, 6 reach private settings; 4 states criminalise in circumstances; one documented arrest (Mar 2025, trespass, handcuffed).
federal_state_facilities.protection: 29 states plus capital district have no mapped ban; the division sits among the most protective with no documented ban.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: The national ban applies inside the protective division; state bans add criminal exposure only in banning states.

care_services.exposure: National order calls minors' care 'mutilation'; Jan 2025 funding freeze; Oct 2025 proposed rule barring public insurance for under-18 care (unresolved); DOJ subpoenaed 20-plus hospitals' youth records.
care_services.protection: Division has comprehensive insurance covering gender-affirming procedures and shield laws/executive orders blocking out-of-state reach; care ban in 27 states does not include this division.
care_services.interaction: Shield protects care sought in the division but cannot displace national funding, subpoena or passport rules.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Dec 2025 reward memo invokes 'radical gender ideology' among violent-extremist viewpoints; May 2026 counterterrorism strategy prioritises groups 'radically pro-transgender'; Jan 2025 order directs law enforcement into schools; 66% poll backing birth-sex document rules.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Memo says rewards are not viewpoint-based and counterterrorism won't target mere disagreement; orders partly enjoined; national employment and hate-crime protections remain.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Official framing raises severity of any outing and energises state-level enforcement, even where unenforced.

minors_guardians.exposure: National document regime governs a child's passport; facility bans reach schools and buildings; Jan 2025 order targets criminal investigation of teachers facilitating social transition; care for minors nationally stigmatised and proposed insurance bar pending.
minors_guardians.protection: Division shield laws and insurance coverage protect care sought there; no documented prosecution of visitors; several orders enjoined.
minors_guardians.interaction: A visiting parent's minor is subject to national documents and facilities while care access depends on the division's shields.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: One documented arrest of a trans woman (Mar 2025) with 24-hour men's-ward holding; 37 states lacked gender-identity bias statutes (2019); no documented rate or pattern of trans-specific street violence.
street_violence_police_response.protection: National hate-crime statute covers gender identity; 23 states cover gender identity in bias statutes; division is protective; no national presentation offence or sodomy law.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Thin violence record leaves visitor exposure between an arrest precedent and unknown incidence.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Passport suit and multiple executive-order challenges unresolved; Feb 2026 state document-invalidating law called a template with more bills pending; two division ballot initiatives targeting trans residents due Nov 2026.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Several orders blocked or enjoined; division ranked among most protective with shield laws; legal-aid FAQ and national equality/identity trackers operate.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Remedies are real but contingent on litigation and pending votes; oversight findings have not changed the national document or custody rules.

anchor_checks.comparison: Lower than 0.35-A: both share an unremedied birth-sex facility rule with no presentation offence, but this dossier adds a traveller-facing entry regime (sex-doubt refusals, fraud ineligibility, blocked passports), a conversion-therapy custody mandate, documented immigration-custody abuse, an arrest with men's-ward holding, and official threat-framing. Pending litigation and protective states keep it out of the 0.15–0.25 band.

Similar: 0.25-D combines a universal birth-sex facility/hospital rule with fraud-charge police pressure and rejected complaints — mirrored here by the facility regime plus sex-doubt/fraud entry screening and custody abuse. Marginally above it because no routine police extortion or hospital-ward directive is documented and courts do enjoin several orders; marginally below on breadth of official hostility.

Lower than 0.45-A: that anchor's only exposure is a national birth-sex bathroom rule in publicly funded buildings with otherwise polite society, prosecution of an assault and no offence. This dossier layers document/entry exposure, custody conversion therapy, immigration-custody violence, a criminal-traverse arrest and multiple state bans on top of the same facility rule.

parsed.synthesis: The traveller encounters one system: protective division laws (shields, insurance, prison care orders) sit under a national regime that governs the moments a visitor actually faces — visa adjudication and document checks, federal buildings, and any detention. National exposures are universal and unremedied: sex-doubt refusals with fraud exposure, blocked markers, government-facility exclusion nationwide, conversion-therapy corrections policy and abusive immigration custody. State bans and one arrest add criminal reach in some units; the division buffers street and care life but not entry, federal facilities or federal custody. Litigation, enjoined orders and shield laws are genuine but partial mitigation; pending ballot initiatives could erode the local buffer further.
